縫why the seams mattered

the machine could not lie yet

In 2015 an engineer ran an image-classifier backwards and the clouds sprouted dog faces. Nobody chose that aesthetic. It was the network's actual texture — perception amplified until it hallucinated, seams showing, every swirl an honest confession of what the machine had been fed and how badly it wanted to see it everywhere. The internet called the creatures puppyslugs. For about four years, that was AI art: nightmare cats drawn from four lines, faces that melted between frames, flesh that would not resolve into bodies. The glitch was not a bug in the art. The glitch was the art.

Then the models learned hands, learned text, learned tastefulness — and every seam they closed made the images more impressive and less honest. What was lost was not weirdness for its own sake. It was legibility: you could see the machine thinking, and it could not pretend otherwise. This room keeps that testimony. The frames below hold the era's relics; the engine beneath holds the era itself, still running, still unable to lie.

take your dream home ↓ (it is born public domain)

honesty about the machinery: this is the same mathematics as Google's 2015 “Inceptionism” — iterative gradient ascent amplifying what a trained convolutional network perceives — run on MobileNet v1 (half a million parameters, ~2 MB of weights, self-hosted here, Apache-2.0), not the original Inception network. a much smaller brain, the same dream. it runs entirely on your device.

They fixed the seams. The dreaming didn't stop; it just learned to pass.
This room remembers when it couldn't.
